nodes.label: Layered AI/SDD workflow (Master Spec → Graphify → OpenSpec → Implementation → verify → archive)
nodes.norm_label: layered ai/sdd workflow (master spec → graphify → openspec → implementation → verify → archive)
nodes.rationale: Layers exist so agents can work with a large project without repeatedly scanning the entire codebase or turning one giant document into an unmanageable implementation prompt; each layer (target-state spec, current-structure graph, active change scope, implementation) has a distinct responsibility.

nodes.label: Block rendering pipeline (Payload Block → Resolver → View Model → Renderer → Section)
nodes.norm_label: block rendering pipeline (payload block → resolver → view model → renderer → section)
nodes.rationale: Separates the CMS schema for a block (manual vs automatic selection) from the rendered UI Section, so a Section never needs to know whether its data came from manual or automatic content selection; unknown blocks log and skip instead of crashing the page.

nodes.label: Tag-based cache and targeted revalidation
nodes.rationale: Using conceptual cache tags (post:{id}, category:{id}, home, navigation, footer, settings) instead of full rebuilds lets publish/update operations invalidate only the dependent content, while Draft Mode must never serve stale public cache to a previewing editor.

nodes.label: Data Access Layer (src/lib/data)
nodes.rationale: Centralizing Payload queries in one layer (getPostBySlug, getLatestPosts, searchPosts, etc.) keeps presentational components query-free and allows the backend to be swapped without touching UI components.

nodes.label: Payload/Next.js separation of responsibilities
nodes.rationale: Payload decides what content exists and its order; Next.js decides how it looks. This split keeps the CMS from emitting arbitrary CSS/HTML/scripts and keeps presentation logic out of the CMS, preventing an uncontrolled visual builder and preserving a consistent editorial design system.

nodes.label: React Server Components by default
nodes.rationale: Minimizes client-side JavaScript and supports progressive enhancement; only components with a genuine browser need (mobile nav, share actions, carousels, accordions) become Client Components.

nodes.label: Project skills routing/precedence policy
nodes.rationale: Loading every installed skill for every task would duplicate guidance, create conflicting heuristics and waste context; routing precedence (Master Spec/OpenSpec > project architecture > most task-specific skill > broad audit skill) keeps only materially relevant skills active.

nodes.label: Source-of-truth conflict priority order
nodes.rationale: Establishes a deterministic precedence (Master Spec > active OpenSpec change > existing verified implementation > tool/skill guidance > agent judgment) so that when instructions conflict, agents resolve deterministically instead of guessing or introducing a third architecture.
